title: Wagertech Internal Sync

items.topic: Redeposits discovery session held
items.statement: Jumpr held a discovery session on redeposits with WagerTech the day before (Sep 16). A WagerTech lead asked to schedule a follow-up for Monday.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um okay so aside from that uh let's talk about wager tech. So we had our discovery yesterday on um was a redeposits. Um looks like they saw some messages from a lead to uh schedule followup for Monday.

items.topic: Offer times for Monday follow-up
items.statement: Kobi will send WagerTech times for the Monday follow-up. He may move the internal morning meetings if that time works better for WagerTech.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um I'll thunder with some times. We'll try to I might move around our meetings in the mornings if that time works out better for them so we can get it out of the way. So just heads up.
items.asr_note: 'I'll thunder with some times' = probably 'I'll send them some times' [ASR?]

items.topic: Confirm commercial terms design with Emily
items.statement: The commercial terms design was presented to WagerTech on the prior Friday. Kobi will get a thumbs-up from Emily that there are no red flags before the build is scoped and assigned.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, and then some outstanding items on my end. Um, the commercial terms uh, design that we talked to them about on Tuesday. Uh, no, not on Tuesday, on Friday. Um, I think I'm just waiting to just get a thumbs up from Emily on if we're good to proceed. and uh scope that out and uh assign that out for somebody to build. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, I don't I think it's fine, but I'm just going to do like a quick check with her just to make sure that there's no red flags before we spend the time to build.

items.topic: Commercial terms as custom object
items.statement: Kobi expects the commercial terms design to be built as a custom object. This depends on Emily's confirmation.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think it's going to be a custom object.

items.topic: CMS API docs received, credentials pending
items.statement: WagerTech sent the CMS API documentation the day before. The sandbox credentials were not yet received and were expected that day.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, and then the API documentation we got yesterday. Um, we still don't have the sandbox credentials, but we're supposed to get it today.

items.topic: Cedrick to start CMS integration
items.statement: When the sandbox credentials arrive, Cedrick will shift focus to the CMS integration. The API PDF is in the WagerTech channel and Kobi will send a Google Doc copy.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, as soon as we get that, um, Cedric, that's probably where you're going to shift focus and we'll get get that like CMS integration going. Um, I there's a PDF in the uh in the Wagertech channel if you want to take a look. um if you have time today also moved it to like a Google doc I think so can send that over as well.

items.topic: Supported markets build options
items.statement: Two build options for supported markets: a multi-select picklist plus formula (quicker, but manually maintained by WagerTech and can drift), or a related object plus flow validation (stays accurate, more effort). Taryn needs Emily to say if manual maintenance is acceptable and if it must be reportable.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: so multi-pick list and formula which is going to be quicker but the caveat is that it would have to be manually maintained on their side so it could drift out of sync and then the other way is a related option. check in plus flow validation which stays accurate but obviously it's going / Taryn Reithofer: to be more effort to build. So I think those two options would satisfy what they want but I think I just wanted to ask her a couple questions like is she okay with it being manually maintained? / Taryn Reithofer: Is this just like a quick reference or does she need to report on it?
items.asr_note: 'supportive markets' (line 307) = supported markets [ASR?]; 'related option. check in' = probably 'related object/junction' [ASR?]

items.topic: Taryn to ask Emily on supported markets
items.statement: Taryn will ask Emily her questions on the supported markets build, then tell Cedrick the answer and close the item.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Um, I think I've got a few questions that I want to ask Emily to really know what we should do for the uh supportive markets build. / Taryn Reithofer: Stuff like that. So once we have those answers then um I'll close I'll close that out.

items.topic: Supported markets mockup in partial sandbox
items.statement: Cedrick built the supported markets mockup in the partial sandbox as a multi-select picklist.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: When you did that mockup, did you actually do it in the sandbox or was that just like / Cedrick Infantado: Yeah, it's in the partial sandbox. / Taryn Reithofer: partial sandbox? / Cedrick Infantado: So I just created a mp list for that.

items.topic: Keep redeposits/payouts backlog stories
items.statement: The mid-August redeposits and payouts backlog stories stay for now, because they came from WagerTech's operator/partner page mockups. After the redeposits design is done, the team will cancel or merge them.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Should we just like scrap those and start over with all this new information now or do you still want them to be there? / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we should keep them for now because they came out of the design mockups that they shared with us for like the operator partner pages, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: once we hash out the design for the redeposits. we can like either cancel or merge them together if needed. / Kobi Kunasekaran: stories were for. So we keep them for now. We clean it up once uh once everything else is done.

items.topic: Primary email blank banner not needed
items.statement: Emily asked for a banner on the player when primary email is blank. A test showed validation stops creating or clearing a player without primary email, so Jumpr considers the banner unnecessary.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Emily had suggested that we have a fraud flag banner and also a primary email banner that shows under the condition if the primary email is blank. Um, but I'm just a little bit confused on that and maybe I'm missing something, but the primary email is required on creation. / Kobi Kunasekaran: No. Okay. So we have validation errors. / Kobi Kunasekaran: but it looks like we've prevented that from happening. So an error message won't be necessary in this case.

items.topic: Tell Emily blank email cannot occur
items.statement: Taryn will tell Emily that a blank primary email should not happen and show her a screenshot of the validation error on create or clear.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, so I think yeah, I think what what you have in there like you just let her know that it it's we are like maybe show her the screenshot of the error when somebody tries to create a record without an email or tries to update a record and clear the email and let her know like it's not a scenario that should happen. / Taryn Reithofer: Hello. Okay. Okay. Okay. Cool.

items.topic: Sandbox test data and change tracking
items.statement: Sandbox player data is test data and no CMS-to-Salesforce data verification is running as far as Kobi knows. When verification starts, test edits must be put on hold or tracked. Taryn should log her test changes in notes or ticket comments.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh it's it's it's it's fine. It's it's all test data anyway. So, um, as long as they're not doing any like ongoing data verification between CMS and, uh, Salesforce, which they're not as far as I know, uh, it's fine. / Kobi Kunasekaran: that's when we'll put a hold or at least like we have to keep track of the changes we're making here, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I I would keep track of it at least in your own notes uh or even like in the comments of um the tickets that you're working on and you're making changes um as a result.

items.topic: Fraud flag banner on player
items.statement: Emily asked for a fraud flag banner on the player profile when fraud is flagged. Jumpr parked it until the driving logic is defined and confirmed with her.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Yeah. Yeah. So I think she wants to to if this uh fraud is flagged. Then she wants it to show on the player banner. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, but how would that work? Cuz you you could have multiple signup records, right? and like if one of them is flag fraud but not the rest like I would define that behavior first and confirm that's what she's looking for

items.topic: Sign-up fraud checkbox driven by fraud button
items.statement: Sign-ups have a fraud checkbox and a fraud details section. The checkbox is set by the fraud button, where the user gives a reason; users do not check it by hand.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: pending, and inactive. Um, we have like a fraud check box in the signups related / Kobi Kunasekaran: like technically they're not going to go in and check that checkbox. The process is through the fraud button. They click on that and then they provide a reason and it'll check the check box on the signup record.
items.critic_note: Timestamp corrected from 00:21:05 to 00:19:47 (nearest timestamp line before line_start 421). Quote, firmness and feature_area verified.

items.topic: Player ban reasons vs simple ban
items.statement: Unclear if player ban has reason codes. Kobi thought fraud was a ban reason; Taryn believes (90% sure) referrer kept ban reasons including confirmed fraud, but player was kept as a simple ban without reasons. Taryn will verify the ticket offline.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: if I'm not mistaken, like we decided on the ban and one of the banned reasons was fraud. / Taryn Reithofer: So I think for for refer we kept the uh ban reasons / Taryn Reithofer: and that one's confirmed fraud there. But for player we decided to keep it simple and not have the reasons and it was just a simple ban. / Kobi Kunasekaran: you can check let's check this like outside like let me know loop back around on this.
items.supersedes_hint: Possible conflict with an earlier sync decision (about a month earlier) that player ban has no reasons; not resolved in this meeting.

items.topic: How fraud drives player status/banner
items.statement: Taryn found Joyce's earlier comment that fraud would be inferred from sign-ups (player shows banned, banner says see sign-ups). Kobi said the team must define when a player is marked fraud, the effect on other player statuses, if review is needed, and if two banners (banned and fraud) are redundant.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, but then like you're going to have two banners, right? One that says a player is banned and then one that says uh the account is or the player is fraudulent. So that might be redundant. / Taryn Reithofer: Yeah, I agree. I agree. You know, maybe like I found where Joyce said, she said uh it would just be inferred from the signups that it was flagged for fraud. She said I think it just says banned and we just have a banner and then see signups for more details. / Kobi Kunasekaran: If we're going to infer from signup, then we need to define what that means. like what? So you you you're going to have multiple signups for a player, right? Um at what point does the player get marked as fraud and what implications does it have on the rest of the statuses on the player?

items.topic: Taryn to clarify fraud banner logic
items.statement: Taryn owns confirming the fraud banner behavior with Emily (how it interacts with active, inactive and ban statuses, and when to show or hide it) before adding the banner.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, yeah. Okay. So, uh I'll leave you with that one. Like we'll let's just double check before uh adding it in. And yeah, if it's a matter of like adding the banner in based on the signup, we just need to confirm like what the behavior should be. Like how does that factor in with the with the active status, the inactive status, the ban status, um and when do you show it versus hiding? / Taryn Reithofer: that's in my to-do list.

items.topic: Operator partner relationship story in progress
items.statement: Cedrick is on the final automation of the operator partner relationship user story. Kobi said it looks almost good to go.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: Uh for me I'm still working on the uh operator partner relationship. So I'm on the final um flow or the automation the for automation on that uh user story. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Okay. Awesome. So, this is this looks like it's almost good to go as well.

items.topic: Async flow cannot trigger on create and update
items.statement: Automation 2 (deal operator/partner junction maintenance) runs asynchronously, but Salesforce does not allow the async path with a created-or-updated trigger. The web workaround is two flows, which Cedrick finds hard to maintain.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: So the flow for maintaining the relationship um it should um the trigger should be created or updated. that however if I try to save this one it could throw an error or a system error for a prevention of Salesforce stating that it could be um it should be updated only or the um in simplified terms it can't be both. So it can be either created or just updated. So the solution that I've got from the internet is just to um create two separate uh flow for that.

items.topic: Single flow with early exit decision
items.statement: Do not split into two flows. The flow runs on deal save and a decision at the start compares prior and current operator and partner values and exits when nothing changed, so there is no DML. Cedrick agreed to add the decision.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, okay. I I don't think you need to do two flows. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So while it'll trigger the flow um you could have a deci decision I think that compares the prior value to the current value. So if the prior value of the operator is the same as the current value and the prior value of the partner is the same as the current value then exit the flow / Cedrick Infantado: I'll just have a decision and then move on.
items.supersedes_hint: Replaces Cedrick's two-flow workaround and his proposed subflow approach.
items.critic_note: Timestamp corrected from 00:35:06 to 00:30:26 (nearest timestamp line before line_start 523). Quote, firmness and feature_area verified.

items.topic: Entry condition operator/partner not blank
items.statement: Kobi suggested the flow entry condition be that operator or partner is not blank, as the flow already checks if the junction record exists.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Like do we need to like can we just make sure that uh like the entry condition is that the um I guess the operator or the partner fields are not blank and then if it's not blank then it's going to try to like it'll run through the flow cuz you're checking anyways to see if the relationship exists, right?

items.topic: Freedom to deviate from cloned design
items.statement: The proposed design for the operator partner automation was cloned; Kobi told Cedrick he can build it a different, easier way if he sees one.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean like if if you think there's a better way to do it than how it's proposed cuz uh the design that is proposed like that was uh that was cloned. So if you think there's a different way like feel free to go about it a different way that's easier.

items.statement: Kobi noted the CMS integration may have implications for the relationship flow, but thinks it is fine if the deal is only updated when something changes.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah I have a feeling like if when we do the CMS integration maybe we'll have to think about like if there's going to be implications here, but I I think it's fine.

items.statement: Kobi received WagerTech confirmation on the billing details for the junction records. He still needs to check the notes to see if anything must change.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, we I did get confirmation from them on the billing details for the junction records. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I don't know if there's anything that we need to do as a result. Um, I have to go back through the notes and uh confirm

items.topic: Story for junction billing details
items.statement: Kobi will update or create a story for the junction record billing details and assign it to Cedrick, who accepted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, so I'm going to follow up with I'll probably like update or create a new story for that. Um, and assign it to you. / Cedrick Infantado: Okay, send it to my bucket and I'll I'll take care of it.

items.topic: Replace email automation with scheduled report
items.statement: The user story's fourth automation (an email for deals missing relationship data) is to be skipped and replaced with a scheduled report of deals without partner or relationship IDs. Jumpr agreed this internally because gates should make the case rare; no WagerTech confirmation is in this transcript.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, you know what? Let's let's let's skip that one. Let's skip that. I think what we can do instead of like a flow is just build a report where the relationship or partner info is blank and then set a scheduled report to send that out. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So we can catch it in a report. So we can cancel that uh that requirement. We'll keep it simple.
items.supersedes_hint: Cancels the email-notification requirement (automation 4) in the operator partner relationship user story; replaced by a scheduled report.

Should I include that in my story or no / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um yeah, like maybe just replace it. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, we just create a report to flag the deal uh sorry flag the accounts or the deals like the deals the deals yeah deals without partners or relationship / Kobi Kunasekaran: IDs and then we'll call it a day simple

Um, let me read through them uh again uh and feed in the feedback from uh Emily and Lena on where the billing details should live for direct and then I will go back and figure out the assignments and uh sign that over.

items.topic: CMS integration delay becoming blocker
items.statement: Kobi is worried about the CMS integration timeline: it needs time to test and fix errors, and CMS must then send deal rep assignments. It will become a blocker if it does not start soon.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, okay. Yeah, I'm hoping we get the the CMS integration details soon though, so we can get started on that. That one is uh starting to worry me a little bit just because that it's going to take us some time to / Kobi Kunasekaran: test out and work through and work out the errors and uh we're and then we're going to need to then start setting up CMS sending us the deal rep assignments as well. So, this is going to start to become a blocker if we don't uh start this soon.

items.topic: Inbound DRA handling approach
items.statement: WagerTech's CMS is to create the deal rep assignments, but Salesforce-side handling is not defined: direct upserts by ID, or a staging object like the SLC intake.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: Did we already pro provide the uh our endpoints to them for um bill assignment or are we the one supplying them the dr? / Kobi Kunasekaran: we they are they are supposed to be the ones creating the DRAs but we haven't worked out what that what that looks like uh from like a handling perspective on Salesforce / Kobi Kunasekaran: So I don't know if we need to do anything to that level or if we're good with them just sending the calls to upsert DRAS directly based on the IDs.
items.critic_note: Timestamp corrected from 00:44:09 to 00:43:02 (nearest timestamp line before line_start 646). Quote, firmness and feature_area verified.

items.topic: Build Salesforce-to-CMS deal IDs first
items.statement: The Salesforce-to-CMS integration that sends deal IDs comes first, because CMS needs the deal IDs to send deal rep assignments back. Inbound DRAs are handled after that.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So that's what we kind of I feel like we need to figure out the CMS sorry the Salforce to CMS integration piece first where we're sending the deal ids because that's what the information they're going to need in order to send the DRA back. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So that's why it's kind of data uh queued up sequentially. So if once we figure out CMS's sorry Salesforce's CMS then we'll talk about it coming back in the form of uh DRAS. / Cedrick Infantado: Okay, cool.

items.topic: Taryn to verify player ban-reason decision
items.statement: Taryn will find the earlier ticket to verify if player ban was kept as a simple ban without reasons, and loop back to Kobi outside the meeting.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: I'd have to find the ticket again to verify, but I'm pretty I'm like 90% sure that's what happened / Kobi Kunasekaran: you can check let's check this like outside like let me know loop back around on this. / Taryn Reithofer: Yeah.

items.topic: How player ban reason is captured
items.statement: Kobi does not want the fraud banner to rely on the player fraud checkbox. Open choice: a screen flow captures the ban reason, or the ban button captures a reason code; if a fraud reason is chosen on ban, that could drive the fraud banner. To be confirmed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I wouldn't rely on it being the checkbox. If it if they're gonna ban players, 99% they're gonna need to know like why the player was banned. So, either we would have like a screen flow to drive that behavior and capture the reason or it was supposed to be tied to the uh the ban button along with the reason that comes with the ban. Um, and we just need to confirm either or.

items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: it sounds like like their initial expectation is now being changed through Emily's feedback here based on what she was saying. / Kobi Kunasekaran: take a step back and then before we add the banner because I think she's looking at it in isolation and it might not make sense in isolation. / Taryn Reithofer: and she uh pasted the um prototype again like referencing it but it's so far off now that maybe she's getting / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Like we we moved away from it, right?

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Replaced email notification requirements with a scheduled report flagging deals missing relationship identifiers. / Decisions (Aligned): Replacing Automated Email Requirement with Scheduled Report The team cancelled the automated email requirement and decided to use a scheduled report instead to flag deals without partners or relationship IDs.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So we can catch it in a report. So we can cancel that uh that requirement. We'll keep it simple.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmness: the summary states the requirement as cancelled and replaced. The transcript shows only an internal Jumpr agreement in an internal sync; the requirement is in a client user story and no WagerTech confirmation is on record.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Next steps list has no fraud-flag action for Taryn; Taryn's only Emily action is supported markets. Details: 'Taryn Reithofer and Kobi Kunasekaran ... agreed to clarify behavioral expectations and alignment with Emily before implementation'.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, yeah. Okay. So, uh I'll leave you with that one. Like we'll let's just double check before uh adding it in. ... / Taryn Reithofer: that's in my to-do list.
gemini_disagreements.why: Omission/misattribution: the transcript assigns the fraud banner clarification to Taryn (Kobi: 'I'll leave you with that one'; Taryn: 'that's in my to-do list'). The Gemini Next steps do not list it.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Wagertech API Credentials and CMS Integration Planning: ... Cedrick Infantado will pivot focus to initiate the Content Management System integration ... / CMS Integration Timeline and Sequence: Kobi Kunasekaran expressed concern regarding the timeline for Content Management System integration
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, as soon as we get that, um, Cedric, that's probably where you're going to shift focus and we'll get get that like CMS integration going.
gemini_disagreements.why: Unsupported expansion (added_by critic): no speaker expands 'CMS' in the transcript. Gemini labels it 'Content Management System', which is its own inference and may be wrong for WagerTech's CMS. Do not reuse the expansion.

notes: Internal Jumpr sync (~47 min). Read all 684 lines. Opening chit-chat skipped. Octo/Appto content (Jira migration from Asana to Kanban, Octo data-issue investigation, the related troubleshooting/walkthrough at lines 661-666) belongs to a different client and was excluded per the no-client-mixing rule; the Gemini Next steps items 'Update Appto', 'Demonstrate Board', 'Investigate Data', 'Troubleshoot Issue', 'Provide Walkthrough' are not WagerTech. One passage on internal ticket reassignment/workload (line 329) skipped under rule 5. 'Create Tickets' next step is only vaguely supported (line 659) and was not extracted. No Jira keys heard. Speaker names are WagerTech-side: Emily, Lena, Joyce (mentioned, not present). Supported markets is transcribed as 'supportive markets'. CRITIC: read all 684 lines; all 32 original quotes verified verbatim; timestamps corrected on items 15, 21, 29, 31; added items 33-36 (Taryn ban-reason ticket check, ban-reason capture approach, outdated-prototype risk, relationship story delay); added 1 Gemini disagreement (CMS expansion). Line 258 'things in review' and line 670 Octo-then-WagerTech priority not extracted: board reference is ambiguous between Octo and WagerTech.
